messages.author: d56d7a5d13e2ace8
messages.subject: missing readShapePoly function
parts:
Hi.
I hope you can help me to escape from building a neighboring matrix from scratch on notebook....
I am reusing a old syntax where I was using the following code to build the .INLA file needed to the BYM model:

freg<-readShapePoly("C:/area.shp",IDvar="codigo")

freg<-freg[order(freg$codigo),]

x.nb<-poly2nb(freg)

veins_inla<-nb2INLA("freg.inla",x.nb)


Now, I'm trying to do this and I receive the error "could not find function "readShapePoly""...

I figured out that the function was changed and that it was not just a change of name because I tried to do that and I received de error "Error in st_sf(x, ..., agr = agr, sf_column_name = sf_column_name) :

  no simple features geometry column present"

I don't understand this error because the shapefile has a Shape_Length and a Shape_Area collumn so there are geometry collumns presented on the shapefile.

I kindly ask if you can help me translate that sintax to the new functions.

Best regards,
Claudia Costa

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] missing readShapePoly function
parts:
Hi,

Since the whole maptools and rgdal packages are deprecated and being retired this year, you’ll need to modify code to use sf instead (the sp package will still work, but  it will call sf internally, so it’s safer to do that directly where possible).
sf::st_read() seems to be the closest replacement to readShapePoly, but the syntax will be different.
poly2nb is part of the spdep package, so you may need to check the documentation for that as well.

Finn

>> Since the whole maptools and rgdal packages are deprecated and being retired this year, you’ll need to modify code to use sf instead (the sp package will still work, but  it will call sf internally, so it’s safer to do that directly where possible).
>> sf::st_read() seems to be the closest replacement to readShapePoly, but the syntax will be different.
>> poly2nb is part of the spdep package, so you may need to check the documentation for that as well.
>>
>> Finn
>>
